Notebook 17 · Exploratory development research

Can temporal history recover the missing signal?

Earlier wearable references did not establish a prediction gain. EMA history remains a promising question—not a verified predictive input.

3,706 responses accounted for125 development participants32 final-test participants sealed0 verified online-history rows
1. The problem is not solved by more columns2. Labels, recall and measurement validity3. Which records were available?4. Personalized wearable inputs and recording quality5. Two evaluation tasks, one evidence boundary6. Actual held-out results7. Does physiology add information?8. Calibration, strata and scientific controls9. What to do next
01 / Evidence & findings

The problem is not solved by more columns

Notebook 16 tested longer windows, compact rebalancing, missingness controls and richer representations. No reliable physiological increment emerged. Notebook 17 tests the interpretation of temporal information and a small fixed set of earlier-recording references. It cannot prove why all previous models were weak.

02 / Evidence & findings

Labels, recall and measurement validity

Stored items are 1–5; score=nervous+(6−cope)+(6−control). Morning recalls since waking; Midday/Endday since the last prompt. Alpha and within-person variance describe these responses, not verified wearable predictability.

04 / Evidence & findings

Personalized wearable inputs and recording quality

The original earlier-recording reference excludes the current hour. The new UTC-clock reference uses matching clock phase over the prior seven days, requiring 30 observed minutes on 3 dates. It is not a validated circadian/resting baseline. Rolling 24-hour step-rate changes require supported intervals in both blocks; no complete-day totals are invented.

The successive-window coverage audit was added after the fixed model fits. It compares recorded fixed-hour summaries, not complete interresponse or prompt-recall intervals; it was not used to select predictors or models.

05 / Evidence & findings

Two evaluation tasks, one evidence boundary

Task A: original unseen-participant folds, with earlier unlabeled wearables allowed. Task A online history: distinct setting, blocked until prior answers are known to be available. Task B: at least five verified available calibration answers, then chronological prediction; population parameters must also use only information available before fitting.

The available schema gives potential sequence counts but no verified Task B eligibility. The two tasks are never pooled. A two-point increase is a specified exploratory change target, not a clinical threshold.
